Gardens for After the Sun

Soft petals, evening air, and the plants that make dusk worth waiting for.

WORDS FROM THE WILD SEED CLUB

We often design gardens for daylight. But the hour after sunset has its own palette: pale flowers gather the last of the light, leaves become silhouettes, and fragrance seems to travel farther through cool air.

Think about the view from your favorite evening chair. A sweep of light-colored blooms, a winding path, and the rustle of taller grasses can make a small garden feel like a world apart.

A garden does not need to perform all day to be beautiful. Sometimes its most memorable moment is the quiet one, when everything slows down and the sky turns indigo.

Some things bloom better when left a little wild.
